newsitem.title: DUBAI: Fourteen victims of India crash to arrive in Saudi.
newsitem.headline: Fourteen victims of India crash to arrive in Saudi.

text.p: The bodies of 13 crew members and one Saudi passenger of a Saudi jumbo jet involved in the world's worst mid-air collision over India will be flown to Saudi Arabia on Friday, a Saudi aviation official said on Thursday.

"The bodies of 13 crew members of the Saudi plane...and the body of the Saudi passenger will be handed over to their relatives after their arrival in Saudi Arabia tommorow," Saudi Arabian Airlines director-general Khaled Ben-Bakr told a news conference in Jeddah.

A Saudi Arabian Airlines Corp jumbo jet with 312 people on board and a KazAir Ilyushin IL-76 freighter carrying 37 collided in flight on Tuesday, seven minutes after the Saudi plane had taken off from New Delhi.
A Saudi Arabian airliner landed in New Delhi on Thursday to fly home the bodies of some victims of the collision, an official at Jeddah airport said.

The official said that so far the bodies of 11 Saudis among the 349 people killed in the crash had been identified, including the Saudi passenger, identified as Majdi Mahmoud Arqoubi from the city of Medina.
The Saudi victims included 12 of the crew members, five of them security men.
"Two Saudis have not been found, but we are hoping to find them," said the official.
Ben-Bakr said a Saudi team that helped in the search at the crash scene found a tape recorder in the flight deck and handed it to the Indian authorities.
The Arab News daily said the body of the pilot, Khalid al-Shubaily, 45, had been identified by his brother who flew to New Delhi after the crash.
Ben-Bakr said there were 289 passengers on the Saudi flight -- 230 Indians, 51 Nepalese, three Pakistanis, two Americans, one Briton, one Bangladeshi and one Saudi national.
